classes.name: Topical corticosteroids
classes.description: Topical corticosteroids by potency: hydrocortisone, triamcinolone, fluocinolone, mometasone, betamethasone, fluocinonide, clobetasol, halobetasol, desoximetasone (creams, ointments, lotions, foams, solutions).
classes.plainDescription: A steroid cream or ointment for eczema, psoriasis or rashes.

classes.name: Non-steroid topicals for eczema
classes.description: Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus ointment, pimecrolimus/Elidel), PDE4 (crisaborole/Eucrisa, roflumilast/Zoryve), JAK cream (ruxolitinib/Opzelura), tapinarof (Vtama).
classes.plainDescription: A non-steroid cream for eczema, often for the face or long-term use.

classes.name: Topical acne treatments
classes.description: Topical retinoids (tretinoin, adapalene, tazarotene, trifarotene), clindamycin and benzoyl peroxide combinations, clascoterone (Winlevi), azelaic acid, dapsone gel.

classes.name: Systemic treatment for moderate-to-severe eczema

classes.plainDescription: A shot or pill for eczema that creams have not controlled.

records.verificationNote: Triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% cream read at PDF p.96 (Skin and Mucous Membrane Agents, Anti-Inflammatory Agents): Tier 1, no QL/LD/MB flag. Alternatives read at p.95 (Tier 1, no flags); clobetasol, fluocinonide and halobetasol are high-potency and listed here for completeness. Combination products (nystatin-triamcinolone, hydrocortisone-iodoquinol) excluded from single-agent alternatives. Sig is standard label dosing, not printed in the formulary. Document says: "Kaiser Foundation Health Plan does not have a requirement for PA" (PDF p.6) and "does not have a requirement for Step Therapy" (PDF p.7). Drugs not listed are nonformulary; when a Kaiser or referral doctor determines one is medically appropriate and necessary it is covered by formulary exception (PDF p.7; decision within 72 hours, 24 urgent, PDF p.8). Completeness is ambiguous: p.6 defines the formulary as "the complete list of prescription drugs preferred for use and eligible for coverage" but p.2 says "not an all-inclusive list", so absence is not treated as exclusion. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: policy wording corrected]
